name: Cut tile mosaic
summary: Glazed tiles of one colour are cut into small shapes, and the shapes are set face down in a plaster bed to form a pattern. The bed holds the pieces after it dries.
how: Glaze and fire plain tiles in 5 or 6 colours.
Cut each tile into pieces with a chisel and a hammer.
Lay the pieces face down on a drawn pattern, with joints under 1 mm.
Pour a bed of plaster over the back and let it set.

origin.note: Seljuk builders in Anatolia and Iran cover domes and entrance halls with mosaics of cut, glazed tiles.

adoptions.via: Seljuk builders cut glazed tiles into turquoise, blue and black pieces for domes, arches and walls in Konya and Iran.
Marinid builders in Fez and Meknes cut glazed tiles into small stars and polygons for walls and fountains.
